# 4 Ezra Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 1:6 — "foreign gods" vs. "strange gods"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "strange gods" | Preserves archaic flavor of Latin alienis diis |
| LOGOS | "foreign gods" | Standard modern scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "alien gods" | Vivid modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Foreign gods" (LOGOS). Clearest and most idiomatic in formal English.

---

## 1:9 — "host" vs. "army"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "army" | Direct functional rendering |
| LOGOS | "host" | Retains biblical register |
| PNEUMA | "entire army" | Adds emphasis for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Host" (LOGOS). Preserves biblical register appropriate for narrative about Exodus.

---

## 1:18 — description of manna

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "bread of angels" | Literal translation of panem angelorum |
| LOGOS | "bread of angels" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the bread of angels" | Identical with article |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Bread of angels" — unanimous agreement, minor article variation only.

---

## 1:23 — address to Jacob/Judah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "What shall I do to you, O Jacob?" | Literal, adversarial preposition |
| LOGOS | "What shall I do to you, O Jacob?" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "What am I to do with you, Jacob?" | More idiomatic modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "What shall I do with you" — PNEUMA's preposition "with" is more natural in English while retaining the second-person address.

---

## 1:29 — hen-and-chicks image

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the way a mother hen gathers her chicks under her wings" | Adds "mother" for emotional resonance |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "As a hen gathers her chicks under her wings" — simpler form without the addition of "mother."

---

## 1:34 — the coming people

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a people that-is-to-come" | Hyphenated literal form |
| LOGOS | "a people yet to come" | Smooth formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "a nation yet unborn" | More vivid but slightly interpretive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "A people yet to come" (LOGOS). Accurate and natural without over-interpreting.

---

## Total disagreements: 6
